headline: AWS growth accelerated to 39% with operating income up sharply, but trailing free cash flow turned to a $42.4 billion outflow on AI capex.
summary: Across the quarters since the FY2025 annual report, AWS sales grew 28% in the March quarter, 37% in the June quarter and 39% in the September quarter. AWS operating income rose to $14.2 billion, $16.6 billion and $17.8 billion, against $11.5 billion, $10.2 billion and $11.4 billion a year earlier [1]. AWS operating income grew faster than AWS sales in each quarter, so the segment margin rose and stays above the 36% level in the T1 signpost [1][4]. Cash moved the other way. Trailing twelve-month free cash flow fell from $25.9 billion at March 2025 to $1.2 billion at March 2026 and to an outflow of $42.4 billion at September 2026, as quarterly cash capex rose to $43.2 billion, $53.1 billion and $75.9 billion [1][2]. Yahoo Finance puts net cash at -$157.7 billion at 30 September 2026, just inside the -$158 billion invalidation level for T2 [3][4]. T1, T3 and T4 are intact or strengthened. T2 moves to broken on current evidence. Reported EPS is distorted by Anthropic gains of $16.8 billion in the March quarter and $53.4 billion of non-operating income in the June quarter [1].
results_commentary:
The scorecard has two post-report quarters, labelled Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended 31 March 2026) and Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended 30 September 2026). The June 2026 quarter appears in the earnings releases [1] and 10-Q [2] but not in the scorecard, so it is discussed here as a separate step and is not given its own status. Fiscal year ends 31 December.

Q1 FY2026 (March quarter): Net sales rose 17% to $181.5 billion, or 15% excluding FX [1]. AWS grew 28% to $37.6 billion, the fastest growth in 15 quarters, and AWS operating income rose to $14.2 billion from $11.5 billion [1]. Operating income reached $23.9 billion against $18.4 billion [1]. Cash weakened sharply. Trailing free cash flow fell to $1.2 billion from $25.9 billion a year earlier, because cash capex rose to $43.2 billion from $24.3 billion [1][2]. Management tied the increase mainly to AI infrastructure. Operating cash flow rose 30% on a trailing basis, so the gap is a capex problem, not a cash-earnings problem [1]. Net income of $30.3 billion ($2.78 per share) included $16.8 billion of pre-tax Anthropic gains, so the EPS beat against $1.65 consensus is not an operating signal [1][3]. Gross margin was 51.8% [3].

June 2026 quarter (in releases, not in scorecard): AWS grew 37% to $42.2 billion, with operating income of $16.6 billion against $10.2 billion a year earlier [1]. Net sales grew 20% to $200.6 billion. Prime Day moved into June for most large countries, which flattered this quarter [1]. Cash capex was $53.1 billion against $31.4 billion, and trailing free cash flow turned to an outflow of $7.6 billion [1][2]. Net income of $62.6 billion ($5.75 per share) included $53.4 billion of non-operating income, mainly from Anthropic [1].

Q2 FY2026 (September quarter, scorecard): Net sales rose 12% to $201.9 billion. Management says the Prime Day shift cost about 400 basis points of growth in this quarter [1]. North America grew 6% and International 5% [1]. Operating income was $28.1 billion, a 13.9% margin and the company's highest ever, against $17.4 billion a year earlier [1]. AWS grew 39% to $46.0 billion, with operating income of $17.8 billion against $11.4 billion [1]. Gross margin was 53.2%, against 50.8% a year earlier [3]. Net income fell to $20.7 billion ($1.89 per share) because the year-earlier quarter carried $9.5 billion of Anthropic gains. EPS was 3.5% below the $1.96 consensus [1][3]. Cash capex was $75.9 billion against $34.2 billion, and trailing free cash flow was an outflow of $42.4 billion [1][2]. Yahoo Finance shows -$37.6 billion on its own basis, a difference we cannot reconcile from the sources [3]. Nine-month cash capex of $172.2 billion exceeded nine-month operating cash flow of $113.8 billion by about $58 billion (illustrative, capex basis, not a reported figure) [2].

Trend: Operations are improving and cash is deteriorating. AWS operating income is growing faster than AWS sales, and group margins rose, while the cash conversion gap widened each quarter. Management expects cash capex to meaningfully increase in 2027 [2].

thesis_check.thesis: T1: AWS operating margin will recover above 36% in FY2026 as new infrastructure scales.
thesis_check.signpost: AWS operating margin above 36% in the FY2026 10-K, with AWS sales growth of at least 20%. Interim test: AWS sales growth at least 18% and operating margin at least 35% each quarter (thesis log).
thesis_check.evidence: AWS sales grew 28% in the March quarter and 39% in the September quarter, and AWS operating income grew faster than sales in both quarters, from $11.5 billion to $14.2 billion and from $11.4 billion to $17.8 billion [1]. The June quarter, with AWS sales up 37% and operating income of $16.6 billion against $10.2 billion, shows the same pattern [1]. The FY2026 10-K is not yet filed, so the status is an interim read.

thesis_check.thesis: T2: Free cash flow turns clearly positive in FY2026 as operating cash flow catches up with capex.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2026 free cash flow above $11.2 billion on the 10-K basis, with capex growth slowing. Interim test: trailing free cash flow positive (baseline invalidation: still negative in the FY2026 10-K).
thesis_check.evidence: Trailing free cash flow fell to $1.2 billion at March 2026 and to an outflow of $42.4 billion at September 2026 [1]; Yahoo Finance shows -$37.6 billion [3]. Nine-month cash capex of $172.2 billion exceeded nine-month operating cash flow of $113.8 billion [2], and management expects capex to rise further in 2027 [2]. The current evidence contradicts the claim that FY2026 free cash flow turns clearly positive; the FY2026 10-K will confirm.

thesis_check.thesis: T3: The stock earns its cost of capital only if revenue growth beats consensus for a decade.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2026 revenue growth at or above 15.7% in the FY2026 10-K, and consensus FY2027 revenue not revised down from $960.5 billion. Interim test: reported revenue at or above $829 billion consensus (thesis log).
thesis_check.evidence: Net sales grew 17% in the March quarter and 12% in the September quarter, with the June quarter at 20% [1]. Nine-month growth is about 16% (illustrative, from release figures), above the 15.7% signpost, though the Prime Day shift distorts the quarterly pattern [1]. Consensus FY2026 revenue is $829.2 billion [3]. FY2027 consensus revenue is $960,547.9 million, and consensus FY2027 EPS was revised up 1.5% over 90 days [3]. Reverse DCF now implies 18.9% growth against a 12.3% WACC [3], a slightly lower hurdle than the 19.3% and 12.4% in the baseline [4].

thesis_check.thesis: T4: Gross margin keeps rising despite competitive pressure, supporting profit growth.
thesis_check.signpost: Gross margin above 50% for FY2026 in the FY2026 10-K, with no new legal charge comparable to the $5.2 billion recorded in 2025. Interim test: no new settlement or tax reserve above $2.5 billion (thesis log).
thesis_check.evidence: Gross margin was 51.8% in the March quarter [3] and 53.2% in the September quarter, against 50.8% a year earlier [3]. The releases and MD&A excerpts we reviewed report no new legal reserve or settlement above $2.5 billion, so the legal signpost is untested rather than failed [1][2].

risk_update:
Risks that materialised: capital intensity and funding. Cash capex rose to $43.2 billion, $53.1 billion and $75.9 billion across the three post-report quarters, against $24.3 billion, $31.4 billion and $34.2 billion a year earlier [2]. Long-term debt financing rose: $59.5 billion of debt was raised in the March quarter [2], and Yahoo Finance shows total debt of $271.9 billion at 30 September 2026 against $153.0 billion at FY2025 [3]. Net cash moved to -$157.7 billion [3]. Current ratio fell to 0.99x [3]. Shares outstanding rose 1.2% year on year [3].

New risks: AI investment commitments. The company disclosed $50.0 billion invested in OpenAI preferred stock in nine months, with a further $35.0 billion equity commitment, and $10.0 billion in Anthropic preferred [2]. Returns on these stakes are not in the operating numbers. Reported EPS depends on their marks, with $16.8 billion and $53.4 billion of gains in 2026 quarters [1].

Eased or unchanged: The releases and 10-Q excerpts we reviewed report no new legal reserve, so the T4 legal signpost is untested rather than breached [1][2]. Competition risk is unchanged in the 10-Q risk factors [2].
outlook: Company guidance: the releases give no numerical revenue or margin guidance. The CEO said AWS revenue growth is projected above 40% in both 2027 and 2028 [1], a claim that is management's projection, not guidance. The 10-Q says cash capex will meaningfully increase in 2027 [2]. Consensus, retrieved 25 November 2026 after the 10-K: FY2026 revenue $829.2 billion (+15.7%) and EPS $12.80, with EPS down 0.2% over 90 days; FY2027 revenue $960,547.9 million and EPS $10.67, up 1.5% over 90 days [3]. What would prove the view wrong: AWS growth below 20% or operating income growth stalling (T1 invalidation), or FY2026 free cash flow still negative in the FY2026 10-K (T2). Watch the FY2026 10-K in February 2027 and the Q4 cash capex figure.
